text: Time shuffling, is something we do every year. The simple thing is we move clocks forward one hour in the spring and then put them back one hour in autumn. So we take an hour of daylight from the morning and put it in the evening. It's not standard time. It's a temporary time, which is used for about 8 months or so in most countries. The reason why it was invented is to use the daylight more. Benjamin Franklin suggested it that we wake up earlier. But the modern thing is invented by George Hudson in 1895, to have more daylight after working hours. And then Germany adopted it in 1916 during World War 1 to save coal, because they had fewer lights in the evening. Other countries adopted it and then it became more of a thing. Also in the meantime, standard time became very important because of the railways and factories. Then the second one, actually how it works is that we spring forward. In the spring, we go from two in the morning to three. So we lose an hour. In the fall, we fall back from two to one, and we gain an hour. So we change the sunrise and sunset by an hour. That's why it's darker in the morning in summer. And today, about 70 countries use daylight saving time in some kind of format.
